bindings.rationale: Conventions include the target-dependent peripheral-availability section; read its body before excluding silicon features.
Memory, buses and boot scope includes several parts; target-specific details remain to reconcile.
Flash chapter includes part-specific registers and update operations beyond latency setup.
CRC source scope is related to the selected word-feed workflow, not all configurations.
Power chapter contains part-specific register branches and low-power modes beyond the reviewed subset.
Chapter title explicitly restricts this RCC branch to STM32F42xxx and STM32F43xxx; target is STM32F407VGT6. Its title locators remain in the pinned outline.
Chapter title explicitly includes STM32F405xx/07xx. Only selected clock recipes are currently reviewed.
GPIO chapter applies; package pin/AF and mode completeness remain separate requirements.
SYSCFG chapter has explicit part-specific branches.
Section title names STM32F405xx/07xx and STM32F415xx/17xx.
Section title names STM32F42xxx and STM32F43xxx, outside this target.
DMA source scope; the memory-copy example does not cover every request, channel or operating mode.
DMA2D availability must be reconciled against the target-specific availability table; shared manual coverage is not proof of presence.
Interrupt/event scope extends beyond the existing UART/button example.
ADC scope; internal-reference conversion is only one supported subset.
DAC scope; software trigger does not establish wired analog-output qualification.
DCMI operating modes, package routing and hardware fixture requirements need reconciliation.
LTDC target applicability must be proven from availability evidence rather than inferred from this shared manual.
Advanced timer scope requires explicit PWM, capture, trigger and advanced-mode contracts.
General timer scope extends beyond the selected TIM2 update/interrupt scenario.
Additional timer instances require their own instance/mode requirements.
Basic timer scope; no all-mode qualification inferred from register discovery.
Watchdog configure/refresh is related knowledge only.
Window-watchdog operating requirements remain to author.
CRYP applicability requires part-specific evidence; absence of a selected workflow is not an exclusion proof.
RNG scope includes more than the reviewed PLL/polling mode.
HASH applicability requires part-specific availability evidence.
RTC operating requirements remain blocked.
I2C controller-only knowledge does not cover every mode or a wired slave.
SPI/I2S scope includes mode and pin-route work beyond current polling knowledge.
SAI target applicability requires availability evidence; do not confuse it with SPI/I2S.
USART source scope includes configurations beyond the UART2 scenario.
SDIO card-transfer requirements and hardware setup remain open.
CAN internal loopback is a scoped subset; external bus remains blocked.
Ethernet operating modes, board interface and fixture remain unqualified.
USB FS source scope; endpoint maps, device/host modes and protocol qualification remain open.
USB HS controller scope requires precise PHY/interface and board applicability review.
FSMC memory modes and package interfaces remain open.
FMC target applicability must be reconciled separately from FSMC.
Debug/trace source scope; current probe operations are not all-mode qualification.
Electronic signature requirements and field provenance need explicit normalized records.
Security notice requires review alongside boot/update requirements.
Revision history; retain source identity and change review.
Datasheet introduction.
Part description and family compatibility require exact-part reconciliation.
Functional overview is a capability cross-check; instance/package constraints need body/table review.
Pinouts and alternate functions are package-specific; not every shared-manual pin exists on LQFP100.
Memory map requires exact density and bank constraints.
Electrical conditions and limits require exact voltage, temperature, clock and interface context.
Several package branches occur in this document.
Section title explicitly names the selected LQFP100 package; mechanical and pin constraints remain to review.
Ordering information must be matched to STM32F407VGT6.
Security notice remains part of requirements review.
Revision history.
Application diagrams need visual review; headings do not reconstruct their connections.
Core overview covers several ST parts; exact target options need reconciliation.
Processor, memory and exception requirements exceed current reviewed subsets.
Instruction set, floating-point and privileged behavior require exact core/build assumptions.
Core peripheral mode completeness is not inferred from declarations.
SysTick section relates to selected core timing examples, not every mode.
Revision history.
Errata summary applicability depends on exact silicon revision and operating conditions. Preserve revision cells literally until body/legend review; physical revision remains unspecified.

missing_sources.reason: Part-specific ROM bootloader protocols, routing and update/recovery requirements need their referenced manufacturer application notes.
Board connectivity is a partial reviewed transcription; complete CAD connectivity/assembly and physical revision evidence remain unavailable.
Section outlines do not enumerate all body/table operating modes, instances, constraints and errata workarounds; their normalized requirement inventory is not yet authored.

scope: Manufacturer source-scope reconciliation for STM32F407VGT6/LQFP100. Section bindings are implementing-author editorial routing from source contents, not independent review, exhaustive modes or hardware qualification. Mixed-family chapters and extraction gaps remain open.
